review.workflow.preview.title: Previewing the producer experience
review.workflow.preview.body: This is the frozen version the producer sees. Review controls are disabled in staff preview.
review.workflow.complete.title: Episode approved

review.workflow.final.title: All scenes approved — final approval needed
review.workflow.final.body: Approve the episode to finish the review. This is a separate final action and does not happen automatically.
review.workflow.approver.title: All scenes approved — waiting for an approver
review.workflow.approver.body: Your scene review is complete. A producer approver must give the final episode approval.
review.decision.approvedBody: This decision was saved. You can change it while the review remains open.
review.decision.pendingBody: No decision has been saved for this scene yet.
review.request.placeholder: Be specific about meaning, tone, character voice, or wording…
review.request.help: Your note is sent to Pulsar with this scene and becomes their next action.
review.request.reasonRequired: Add a reason so Pulsar knows what to change.
review.saved.approved: Scene {n} approved. Your decision was saved.
review.saved.alternative: Changes requested for scene {n}. Pulsar has been notified.
review.saveFailed: Could not save the scene decision.
review.finalReady: Every scene is approved. This final action completes the producer review.
review.episodeBlocked.changes: Cannot approve yet: Pulsar must revise {n} scene(s).
review.episodeBlocked.remaining: Cannot approve yet: decide the remaining {n} scene(s).

wb.submit.lines: {n} of {total} lines are ready. Finish every English line before sending this episode.
wb.scene.notReady: {n} line(s) in this scene still need a complete English adaptation.
wb.workflow.start.title: Generate the first English draft
wb.workflow.start.body: Start the AI pass, then review every English line before marking scenes ready.
wb.workflow.blocked.title: English drafting is blocked
wb.workflow.blocked.body: AI is not configured on this server. Ask an administrator to connect the Anthropic API before this episode can move forward.
wb.workflow.edit.title: Finish the English adaptation
wb.workflow.edit.body: {n} line(s) still need complete English text, rationale, or back-translation. Select each highlighted line and finish it.
wb.workflow.readyScenes.title: Review and mark scenes ready
wb.workflow.readyScenes.body: All lines are complete. Review the bilingual result, then mark the remaining {n} scene(s) ready for the producer.
wb.workflow.send.title: Ready to send to the producer
wb.workflow.send.body: Every line and scene is ready. Send this version to freeze it and begin producer review.
wb.workflow.waiting.title: Waiting for producer review
wb.workflow.waiting.body: The submitted snapshot is read-only. No staff action is needed until the producer decides or requests an alternative.
wb.workflow.returned.title: Producer requested changes in {n} scene(s)
wb.workflow.returned.body: Read the producer notes below, create a revision, address each request, and send the new version back.
wb.workflow.approved.title: Producer approved this episode
wb.workflow.approved.body: The approved snapshot is final and ready to export. Create a revision only if a new change is required.
wb.workflow.manual.title: Start a manual English draft
wb.workflow.manual.body: AI is not configured, but you can still continue. Create editable blank lines, then translate each one before marking scenes ready.
admin.episodeNext.start: Create an English draft for {n} line(s)
wb.fork.reviewPending: Wait for the producer to decide the remaining {n} scene(s) before creating a revision.

wb.requests.title: {n} timestamped change request(s)
wb.requests.frozenHelp: The request and exact note are shown below. Create a revision to edit the submitted version.
wb.requests.pendingHelp: The request and exact note are shown below. The producer still has {n} scene(s) to decide; revision editing unlocks when their review is complete.
wb.requests.draftHelp: You are editing the revision. Resolve each note below, mark the scene ready again, then send the new version to the producer.
admin.episodeNext.feedbackPending: {changes} change request received · producer has {remaining} scene(s) left
wb.adapted.manualHint: Use Start manual draft above to create editable English lines without AI.

reviewStudio.revisionThreadHelp: Review the complete change history before approving.
reviewStudio.responsePending: Pulsar has not explained how this request was handled.
reviewStudio.selectedMomentHelp: The request will be pinned to this exact line and timestamp.
reviewStudio.commentPlaceholder: Describe exactly what should change at this moment…
reviewStudio.saved.request: Change request sent at {time}. Pulsar will see it on the same line.
wb.submit.responses: Respond to {n} producer request(s) before sending the revision.

pw.home.title: My titles
pw.home.sub: Localize subtitles, refine the English adaptation, and deliver timed files.
pw.new.title: New title
pw.new.sub: Add a drama series to your catalog. Only its Chinese name is required. You can upload episode videos and subtitles now or add them later.
pw.new.notesHint: Main characters' names, roles and relationships; the adaptation uses this.
pw.upload.title: Upload scripts
pw.upload.hint: SRT / VTT / ASS subtitle files or a TXT script; one file per episode.
pw.steps.label: Workflow
pw.title.noEpisodes: No episodes yet. Add video or subtitles below.
pw.ep.sub: Original on top, adaptation below; every change explains itself.
pw.gen.title: Generate the U.S. adaptation
pw.gen.body: The AI rewrites each line in natural American English — not a translation, but a rewrite of rhythm and tone for U.S. viewers. Every change carries a Chinese explanation, and you can edit any line afterwards.
pw.gen.unmatched: {n} line(s) have no pre-authored translation (demo mode covers the bundled scripts only).
pw.gen.step3: Adapting each line for U.S. viewers
pw.line.pending: This line has not been adapted yet.
pw.alts.none: No more alternatives for this line.
pw.finalize.confirm: Save this version as final? Later edits will start a new draft and keep this approved version intact.
pw.final.banner: This episode is finalized and archived
pw.export.hint: Export the finalized files any time
pw.review.banner: Pulsar submitted this version. Finalize it as is, or edit it yourself first.
pw.alts.suggested: Suggested alternatives — tap to use one
pw.panel.title: Review & edit
pw.cmd.confirm.title: {n} scene(s) left to confirm
pw.cmd.confirm.body: Click any timestamp to review a line — edit it directly or take an alternative; confirm each scene, then finalize.
pw.cmd.ready.title: Ready to finalize
pw.cmd.ready.body: Every scene is confirmed. Finalizing freezes and archives this episode; export any time.
pw.cmd.review.title: Pulsar submitted this version
pw.cmd.review.body: Finalize it as is, or edit it yourself first.
pw.cmd.done.title: This episode is finalized
pw.cmd.done.body: Content is frozen and archived; export the finalized files on the right.
pw.confirm.done: Updated — the script on the left reflects it.
pw.confirm.hint: Edit the line or pick an alternative, then Save line to apply.
pw.confirm.clean: Edit the English above, or view the alternatives.
pw.cmd2.lines.title: {n} line(s) left to adapt
pw.cmd2.lines.body: Click any timestamp — edit the English directly or take an alternative. Finalize once every line is ready.
pw.cmd2.ready.body: Every line is adapted. Finalize to export the English script and the subtitled video.
pw.cmd2.done.body: Frozen and archived. Download the English script and the subtitled video from the rail.
pw.subvid.done: Subtitled video ready ({n} cues) — opened in a new tab.
pw.upload.hint2: One row per episode: set the number, pick that episode's subtitle/script file; video optional.
qc.title: Delivery preflight
pw.upload.hint3: Files are optional now. Ad generation needs episode video; English subtitle adaptation needs a script or subtitle file. Matching filenames, such as ep1.mp4 and ep1.srt, go into the same episode.
pw.upload.pick: Drop all your files here, or click to choose
pw.upload.pickHint: Subtitles and videos together — matched to episodes by filename (ep1.srt, ep1.mp4 …)
pw.slots.missingSub: This episode still needs its subtitle file
pw.gen.nomatch: This script isn't in the demo bank, so demo mode can't adapt it. Ask Pulsar to enable AI adaptation for your workspace.
pw.gen.overrun: taking longer than estimated — still generating…
st.notFinal.title: Finalize the script first, then style the subtitles
st.notFinal.body: Subtitles are built from the frozen, finalized script so later edits can't drift into the delivered video. Finish reviewing and finalize in the episode studio, and this page unlocks.
st.untimed.title: This episode has no timecodes
st.untimed.body: Subtitles need a start and end time for every line. This episode came from a plain-text script (or has no usable lines), so cues can't be generated — episodes ingested from SRT/VTT/ASS files support subtitles. The English script report is still available.
st.noVideo: No video attached — previewing style only
st.render.noVideo: No video on this episode yet — attach one in the episode studio to render the burned video here. The SRT/VTT files below work regardless.
st.retime.body: Each line here starts with an [hh:mm:ss] stamp — an earlier ingest left the timecodes inside the text. One click lifts them into a real timeline (end times from the following line) and, if this episode was finalized, refinalizes it automatically.
st.retime.review: Timeline repaired, but QC found issues to address — review in the episode studio, then finalize again.
st.t.offsetHint: Negative shifts every subtitle earlier (use negative when the audio runs ahead of the subs). Applied once, immediately.
st.t.pickCue: Click a line in the cue sheet below first - then adjust when it appears and disappears here.
st.t.keys: Keys: , and . nudge the selected cue by 100 ms; hold Shift for 500 ms.
st.t.warn.overlap: Cue {n} overlaps the previous by {v} ms
st.t.warn.beyond_video: Cue {n} runs {v} ms past the video
st.t.autosyncOff: Not available yet — contact Pulsar to enable auto-sync for your workspace.
v3.nav.title: Title workspace
v3.revise.help: The approved version stays archived. Your edits continue in a new version.
v3.subtitle.timingHint: Adjust cue timing and resolve timeline issues
v3.subtitle.deliveryHint: Preview subtitle styling and export final files
v3.title.actionHint: These statuses track subtitle preparation, not ad approval.
v3.title.addEpisodesHint: Upload new subtitle or video files
v3.done.body: The script is finalized. Create a new draft to revise it, or continue in Timing & delivery above.
pw.alts.picked: Alternative applied - press the save button below to confirm.
qc.fix.none: Fix with AI - nothing to fix right now
st.acc.timing.sub: Subtitles early or late? Line them up here
st.acc.deliver.sub: The subtitled video and the files
st.suggest.body: The subtitles look uniformly late: the timestamps are rounded to whole seconds (a frame-sampling artifact). Recommended: shift everything 0.5s earlier.
st.t.cue.tip: Click a line in the cue sheet below, then adjust exactly when it appears and disappears here.
st.t.setStart.tip: Make this line appear at the player's current moment
st.t.setEnd.tip: Make this line disappear at the player's current moment
st.t.offset.tip: Shift every subtitle earlier or later together
st.t.loop.tip: Replay the selected line on repeat
st.t.before.tip: Play from 2s before the selected line to hear the entry
st.merge.hint: Two short neighboring cues display together as two rows - on screen longer, less flicker. English-only content.
pw.alts.dir.title: Neither one? Take it another direction
pw.cmd.blocked.title: {n} issue(s) to fix before finalizing
pw.cmd.blocked.body: Preflight found blocking issues. Use Fix or Fix all with AI in the panel, then finalize.
promote.home.title: Ad campaigns
promote.home.sub: Prepare ads, choose and approve them, approve the budget, launch, then review results.
promote.home.emptyTitle: Your first campaign starts with a drama
promote.home.emptyHint: Choose an uploaded title to prepare direct-clip and creator-style ads.
promote.new.title: New ad campaign
promote.new.sub: A campaign is one round of ads for a single drama. Save the brief first, then generate and select ads, approve the content and budget, and submit the round.
promote.new.noTitlesHint: Add a title to your catalog, then return here to plan its ads. You can upload video later.
promote.new.videoRequired: This title needs at least one episode video before ad generation can begin.
promote.new.directionHint: For example: she looks powerless at first, but the audience should sense she is in control.
promote.new.exclusionsHint: Characters, episodes, plot reveals, claims, or visual moments to avoid.
promote.new.spoilerHint: This controls which moments can become hooks—not just the copy.
promote.new.outputHint: Saving creates a draft. On the next screen, generate five ad proposals with opening lines, captions and source clips, then choose which to test.
promote.workspace.sub: Review the hypothesis behind each ad—not just whether the clip looks good.
promote.workspace.readyHint: Generate five ads from the uploaded episode videos, then choose the ads for your first test. Review results before preparing another round.
promote.workspace.caption: Post caption
research.market.title: US overview
research.market.sub: Public charts from ReelShort and DramaBox through one story-type taxonomy: what is prominent, what the charts are made of, and where your catalog fits.
research.market.noData: No published market snapshot. Run the crawl to create one.
research.market.firstObservation: First observation day; change columns turn on with the second.
research.section.tropes: What the charts are made of
research.section.tropesSub: Share of the 50 hottest titles in the current filter that carry each trope.
research.section.topSub: Within-platform heat: view percentile lifted by chart position.
research.section.studiosSub: As the platform shows them. DramaBox names a publisher; ReelShort names none, only its own originals.
research.formats.note: Medians per platform with sample sizes: episodes per listing, first paid episode, episode length (basis named, never pooled).
research.col.title: Title
research.evidence.legend: Every number carries its source. Observed: read from the platform's page. Inferred: derived by our rules. Estimated: a model's estimate. Partner-reported: told to us by a producer.
research.heat.note: Heat is relative within a platform (0 to 100). Raw views count different things on different platforms and are never compared across them.
research.personal.title: For your studio
research.personal.sub: Based on the tropes you told us you produce.
research.personal.producingHot: You produce it, the charts show it
research.personal.hotNotProducing: The charts show it, you don't list it
research.personal.producingCold: You produce it, thin on the charts
research.onboard.banner: Answer a few questions and this desk personalizes to your tropes.
research.onboard.title: Company profile
research.onboard.sub: We use this to filter the market for you. It is never shown to other producers.
research.onboard.tropesHint: Choose 1–12 story types. You can change these later.
research.onboard.marketsHint: Choose your target release markets (up to 8).
research.onboard.readOnly: Staff preview: the profile is read-only here.
research.onboard.viewerOnly: Only reviewer or approver roles can edit the profile.
research.title.notFound: This listing is not in the current snapshot.
research.mine.title: My titles
research.mine.sub: Your titles against the market. Localization and test tools live inside each title.
research.mine.vsMarketSub: Each title's tropes scored against the prominent-listing share; open a title for comparable listings and why.
research.mine.untagged: No tropes recognized. Add a synopsis to match.
research.mine.perfEmpty: No US performance data yet. Import a distribution or platform report and each title compares to the market on comparable definitions.
research.hooks.title: Hooks that are working
research.hooks.sub: The opening sentence of the hottest titles' blurbs: what grabs a viewer before episode one.
research.market.invalid: The published snapshot failed validation and is not shown. See Data & Sources.
research.scope.value: English public catalogs · audience geography unknown
research.state.collectingHint: Needs a second observation day to show change.
research.state.noCatalog: Shown once you add a title
research.section.prominentSub: Within-platform prominence: view percentile or chart position, whichever is higher. Not momentum.
research.section.insightsSub: Templated from the snapshot; each cites the listings it was computed from.
research.section.storyMixSub: Share of the prominence cohort carrying each trope. Multi-label: shares sum above 100%.
research.section.yourTitlesSub: Tagged from your synopses; similarity to prominent listings, not success probability.
research.section.newListingsSub: Marked new by the platform in this crawl. "First seen by us" starts with the second observation day.
research.section.companiesSub: As the platform shows them, with the role kept. DramaBox names a publisher; ReelShort names none beyond its own originals.
research.insight.tropeLift: "{trope}" is {lift}× as common among prominent listings as in the tracked sample ({inCohort} of {cohort} vs {titles} of {sample}).
research.insight.paywallGap: {a} puts the first paid episode at {aMedian} (n={aN}); {b} at {bMedian} (n={bN}).
research.insight.newListings: {platform} marks {count} listings as new in this crawl.
research.insight.audienceSplit: {share} of tracked {platform} listings are positioned 女频 (n={n}). Platform shelving, not audience data.
research.explore.title: Explore
research.sort.title: Title
research.noResults: No listings match. Reset the filters or search a different term.
research.viewsPooledNote: Views columns are platform-specific counters and are never pooled.
research.role.note: A publisher label is not the production studio. Neither platform exposes who made a title.
research.audience.note: Platform audience positioning, not protagonist gender and not measured demographics.
research.prominence.note: Prominence is relative within a platform (0–100). Raw views count different things on different platforms and are never compared across them.
research.onboard.audienceHint: How you position your titles (女频 / 男频), not who watches them.
research.title.similarNote: Shared story types from platform tags and synopsis classification. Similarity does not establish that two listings are the same drama.
research.title.trendsEmpty: Trends need at least two observation days; there is {days} so far. Nothing is invented before then.
research.title.rankMove.absent: Not on a chart on either day
research.title.counter.anomaly: Counter decreased ({start} → {end}); treated as an anomaly, not negative demand.
research.title.counter.noBaseline: No baseline: first seen this crawl.
research.title.counter.noCounter: No comparable counter on both days.
research.title.creativeEmpty: Ad creative observations need a connected source (see Data & Sources). Below are premise sentences from the synopsis, not tested hooks.
research.title.sourcesNote: Source field, unit and read time of every number on this page.
research.title.identityNote: This is one platform listing. The same drama may appear elsewhere under another title; similarity is not identity.
research.sources.title: Data sources & definitions
research.sources.sub: What every metric means, where it comes from, how it is defined, and its current state. Credentials and operational logs are not here.
research.sources.question: Question
research.geo.unknown: Unknown (an English page does not establish a US audience)
research.premise.title: Premise examples from prominent titles
research.premise.sub: The first sentence of each synopsis. Examples of how a premise is stated, not tested hooks: no creative-outcome evidence exists here.
research.watch.empty: Nothing watched yet. Watch a listing from its page; rank and counter changes appear here once a second observation day exists.
research.watch.readOnly: Reviewer or approver roles can watch listings.
research.shortlist.title: Launch-test shortlist
research.shortlist.sub: An explained hypothesis, not a probability of success. Formula v{version}: comparables (0–50), rights window (±), localization readiness (0–20), your constraints (±10), own evidence (+5).
research.shortlist.reason.comparables: Market match {score}: {n} comparable prominent listings, {hot} prominent tropes
research.shortlist.reason.untagged: No tropes recognized in the synopsis
research.shortlist.reason.rightsOk: License window covers today (until {end}, as you reported)
research.shortlist.reason.targetsUS: You listed the US as a target market
research.shortlist.reason.notTargetingUS: US not among your target markets ({markets})
research.shortlist.reason.noProfile: Target markets not set in your studio profile
research.shortlist.reason.ownReports: {n} imported report rows link to this title
research.shortlist.reason.noReports: No imported performance for this title
research.reports.title: My reports
research.reports.sub: Import your own distribution or platform reports as CSV. Rows are validated before anything is saved; a batch can be reverted. Only your company sees them.
research.reports.columns: Expected columns: title, platform, period_start, period_end (optional), metric ({metrics}), value, currency (for revenue/spend). Chinese headers are recognized.
research.reports.unmatched: {n} titles not in your catalog (imported without a link)
research.reports.readOnly: Reviewer or approver roles can import reports.
research.mine.perfFrom: From your reports (latest period per metric)
v3.dramaLibrary.sub: Every title you have in contact with Pulsar. Connect with Stage, our streaming platform, to see how they perform.
v3.dramaLibrary.emptyHint: Once connected with Stage, this page lists your titles with us and their viewing metrics.
promote.new.pickHint: Ads are generated from this drama's episodes.
admin.promote.title: Promote desk
admin.promote.sub: Every producer ad campaign: what it needs from Pulsar, and how its TikTok launch is doing.
admin.promote.empty: No campaigns yet. They appear here when a producer starts an ad campaign.
admin.promote.launch.submitted: Created on TikTok with {n} ads; TikTok is reviewing them. Nothing to do unless the review stalls.
admin.promote.launch.launching: The launch engine is creating the objects on TikTok. If this stays here for more than ten minutes, the scheduler adopts it; Sync now forces it.
admin.promote.launch.live: Delivering on TikTok. Metrics are read back hourly.
admin.promote.launch.failed: The launch failed. Fix the cause (the note says what TikTok answered) and retry — the same launch record resumes; no second campaign is created.
admin.promote.launch.waiting: Nothing to launch yet — the producer has not submitted this campaign.
admin.promote.creatives.sub: Answer each change request with a revised ad; the producer can choose it or request another change.
admin.promote.revise.caption: Caption
admin.promote.revise.closed: Review is closed for this campaign; revisions need a new round.
promote.workspace.roundNote: Generate 5 ads, choose which to test, then review results before the next round.
pw.cmd.explain.title: {n} line(s) missing their adaptation notes
pw.cmd.explain.body: These AI rewrites lack their Chinese rationale or back-translation, so finalize is held. Open each line and pick an alternative or edit it once by hand.
pw.err.aiOff: AI rewriting is not available in demo mode. Contact Pulsar to enable AI adaptation for your workspace.
ux.company.sub: Your story interests guide the market brief. Your catalog and reports stay within your company.
ux.overview.sub: Find overseas dramas worth studying, and connect them to your next release.
ux.profileSaved: Company profile saved. Your recommendations are up to date.
ux.filters.counter: Choose a platform to sort by views or saves.
ux.scope: English public catalogs · viewer location unknown
ux.dramas.personal: Examples matching your company’s story interests and the filters above.
ux.dramas.all: A selection based on within-platform visibility, not a global ranking.
ux.storyBasis: Among prominent titles in the selected market filters. Your company’s interests are highlighted; titles can have several story types.
ux.nextStep.sub: Connect a title in your catalog to a useful next action.
ux.catalog.sub: Your titles, comparable overseas stories, and the materials you have ready.
ux.noComparable: Add a synopsis to find story comparisons.
ux.rights.note: Check territory rights and episode approvals on the title before planning a release. Uploads alone do not establish release readiness.
ux.market.intent: Your target markets express intent; public catalog counters do not measure these audiences.
ux.volume.note: Descriptive company information; not used to score recommendations.
ux.counter.note: A counter observed on this platform’s public listing.

sim.title: What should Harborlight produce next?
sim.notice: Fictional company · AI-authored original scripts · No videos or performance data. This case is separate from your company and catalog.
sim.mission: Choose one concept for a two-week development sprint, then decide whether to commission a pilot. Success today means a defensible shortlist and a specific test—not a prediction of a hit.
sim.identity: Harborlight Stories / 海光影业 · Hangzhou · Independent producer. Chen Lin, co-founder and development lead, prepares the slate; the founder approves production spend. A US freelance story editor reviews dialogue and cultural context.
sim.audienceBody: US English-speaking women aged 25–44; romance with capable heroines. Hypothetical audience intent, not measured demographics. Seek a platform licensing partner; no existing US distribution agreement or owned consumer app.
sim.resourcesBody: Eight-person core team; strong contemporary romance experience, two controllable interiors and a bilingual script editor. No established US casting or location partner. Planning assumptions: $15k development cap, $180k production ceiling per title, 10 shoot days, 6 principal cast, no stunts/VFX. Budgets are invented case constraints, not market benchmarks.
sim.slateBody: Three unproduced original concepts, no footage, no licenses sold. Working format: 40 × 90-second episodes, subject to buyer feedback. English originals are preferred over dubbing for this experiment. Avoid child performers, medical claims and expensive public locations. Buyer terms, acquisition costs and revenue are unknown.
sim.workflowBody: 1. Read the company brief. 2. Compare the three concepts against those constraints. 3. Read two opening episodes. 4. Inspect relevant market titles and record what is actually observed. 5. Pick a development candidate and write the uncertainty that could reverse your decision.
sim.concepts: Three concepts competing for one slot
sim.reason: Why this title—and what would change your mind?
sim.placeholder: Example: Contained locations fit our team. Before greenlight, test whether viewers understand the contract twist without exposition.
sim.empty: Select a concept above to build a decision brief.
sim.temporary: Exercise only. Selection and notes stay in this page until you leave or reload; download to keep them. No title is commissioned.
sim.inference: What the product should help you conclude
sim.inferenceBody: A similar title is a research lead. Its synopsis can reveal a story device; its visible counters describe platform activity. Neither proves why audiences watched, US demand, profitability, or buyer appetite. A useful next step connects a specific story device to your script, your constraints, and a test that could reject the idea.
sim.contract.name: The Exit Clause
sim.contract.premise: An indebted event planner agrees to a staged engagement, then discovers the contract gives her control of the family business if the groom walks away.
sim.contract.fit: Best first development candidate under these invented constraints: adult cast, office/apartment interiors, and a recurring negotiation engine. Her bargaining power needs to drive the romance.
sim.contract.risk: A legal twist may require too much explanation. A familiar billionaire setup needs a distinctive heroine goal; a synopsis cannot demonstrate audience appetite.
sim.contract.test: Table-read both openings with five target-language readers. Ask them to retell her leverage and choose which question makes them want episode 3. Small qualitative test, not demand validation.
sim.receipt.name: The Last Receipt
sim.receipt.premise: A hotel bookkeeper framed for theft returns as the anonymous buyer of the hotel, but the only witness who can clear her is her former fiancé.
sim.receipt.fit: A concrete evidence trail gives each episode a reveal. A dressed office can double as hotel administration; a luxury lobby and crowds would exceed this case’s location plan.
sim.receipt.risk: Revenge could crowd out the romance. Hotel scale may exceed the budget; buyer interest and production quotes remain unverified.
sim.receipt.test: Rewrite the pilot using only two interiors. Ask a line producer for a scene-level estimate and readers whether they believe her evidence is strong enough to act.
sim.midnight.name: Before Midnight, Again
sim.midnight.premise: A night-shift concierge repeats the hour before a tenant disappears. Each reset saves a clue but erases one memory of the man helping her.
sim.midnight.fit: A contained supernatural romance offers a different slate option. Repeated sets help, but continuity and consistent reset rules require more development effort.
sim.midnight.risk: The reset may confuse viewers in 90 seconds. Disappearance scenes must stay off-screen to avoid action costs; differentiation does not establish commercial potential.
sim.midnight.test: Storyboard the reset without VFX. Test whether readers can state what persists and what is lost; hold production until the rules survive a cold read.
sim.contract.script:
EPISODE 1 — OFFICE, NIGHT
MAYA places an unpaid invoice between herself and ADRIAN.
MAYA: You want a fiancée. I want my crew paid. Those are different contracts.
ADRIAN: Thirty days. Two dinners. No one gets hurt.
She crosses out a paragraph.
MAYA: Then why does this say I owe you if I leave?
He slides over a pen.
ADRIAN: Write something fair.
MAYA: Whoever walks away loses control.
His smile disappears when she turns to the signature page.
CUT: Both signatures sit beneath the company seal.

EPISODE 2 — OFFICE, MORNING
Adrian’s sister EVE reads the agreement.
EVE: You used the shareholder template?
MAYA: He said write something fair.
EVE calls Adrian. Speakerphone.
ADRIAN: Last night was a mistake. We’re done.
Eve covers the phone and points to a clause.
EVE: If he terminates, your proxy activates.
MAYA looks at the invoice, then the board meeting invitation.
MAYA: Tell him I’ll see him at nine.
The phone lights up: BOARD VOTE — REMOVE MAYA’S CREW.
sim.receipt.script:
EPISODE 1 — HOTEL ACCOUNTS OFFICE, DAY
NORA returns her staff badge. Manager GRANT drops a receipt on the desk.
GRANT: Your signature. Missing cash. Be grateful we’re keeping this quiet.
NORA: That printer was replaced on Tuesday. This is dated Monday.
He tears the receipt in half.
GRANT: Then prove it.
Nora pockets the lower half. Outside, her phone rings.
LAWYER (PHONE): The purchase closed. Do you want the staff told who owns the hotel?
NORA: Not yet.

EPISODE 2 — SAME OFFICE, EVENING
Nora requests the archived printer log. Her former fiancé ELI blocks the cabinet.
ELI: If Grant sees you, you’re finished.
NORA: He already finished me. Move.
Eli opens the cabinet. The folder is empty except for an envelope bearing his name.
NORA: You signed the report?
ELI: I signed to keep you out of court.
She unfolds a copy. The timestamp matches the torn receipt.
NORA: Then why did you sign it before the money disappeared?
sim.midnight.script:
EPISODE 1 — APARTMENT CONCIERGE DESK, NIGHT
11:59. JO finds a key with a red thread. BEN arrives, breathless.
BEN: Don’t give that to room twelve.
JO: You said that yesterday.
BEN: No. I said it in the last hour.
The desk phone rings. A woman whispers: He’s outside my door.
Jo reaches for the emergency button. Midnight. Blackout.
11:00. The lights return. The red thread is tied around Jo’s wrist.
Ben enters.
JO: Do I know you?

EPISODE 2 — CONCIERGE DESK, NIGHT
Ben sets down a notebook in Jo’s handwriting.
JO reads: Objects in my pocket stay. Memories of Ben don’t.
JO: Convenient story.
She tears a corner off a blank page and puts it in her pocket.
BEN: We have fifty-eight minutes.
JO: Then we use them to find her.
The phone rings early. Same woman.
WOMAN: This time don’t trust the man at your desk.
Jo looks down. Ben has the matching red thread around his wrist.

an.ep.revenueBasis: Directly mapped episode revenue sums to {mapped}; the title's IAP gross in the period is {total}. Coins bought but not yet redeemed stay unmapped.
an.ep.noAttribution: Episode attribution is not delivered for this listing
an.ep.noAttributionBody: The source reports listing totals only. Per-episode starts, continuation, unlocks and revenue are unavailable, not zero.
an.ep.def.entry: Mid-title entry: a viewer who starts episode N without having started N−1 within the window counts as a starter of N but never in N−1's continuation numerator.
an.ep.def.replays: Replays: starts count every playback event; unique starting viewers count a person once per day; completion rate uses starts.
an.ep.def.sequence: Out-of-sequence viewing: continuation only counts N+1 started within {days} days after N; watching N+1 first and N later does not count. Cross-episode identity is not reconciled across the period.
an.ep.def.uniques: Unique starting viewers are daily-unique and summed over the period; a person active on two days counts twice in this column (the title's period-unique viewers are on Overview).
an.ep.def.sample: Small sample: under {min} unique starting viewers in the period; flags are suppressed for such rows.
an.acq.none: No campaign has run for this title
an.acq.noneBody: Acquisition figures come from campaign result rows. Create a test to get spend, impressions, clicks and, where reported, attributed users.
an.acq.titleRevenue: Title IAP gross in this range
an.acq.unattributedNote: Revenue not attributed to a campaign is unattributed, not organic: this source cannot tell where it came from.
an.acq.benchmark: Benchmarks: hook hold ≥ {hold}%, CTR ≥ {ctr}% (shared with US launch priority).
an.acq.rows: Built from {n} result row(s) of this campaign
an.acq.roasNote: attributed gross sales / spend; not profit
an.reason.componentUnavailable: this component is not delivered for the listing
an.reason.immature: no cohort has reached this horizon yet
an.reason.notSettled: no settled days in this period
an.reason.attributionNotReported: attribution not reported for this campaign
an.reason.noAttributedRevenue: no attributable revenue: ROAS not shown
an.note.noEpisodeAttribution: listing totals only; no per-episode data
an.catalog.sort.name: name
an.catalog.caption: Ranking: {basis} in USD over {range}. Each title’s period ends on its latest reporting day; compare the dates and coverage shown in each row.
an.catalog.footNote: Titles without a value sort last. The 30-day revenue figure uses viewer groups with a full 30 days of history and shows gross revenue per starting viewer.
tw.nav.label: Title sections
tw.ads.noneYet: No ad campaign on this title yet.
tw.tiktok.notLinked: Link this title to its TikTok listing to see earnings and viewers.
tw.tiktok.awaiting: Linked. The first report has not arrived yet.
tw.tiktok.noValue: No earnings value in this period.
tw.next.firstCampaignHint: Video is available. The next step is a first ad campaign.
pf.title: My catalog
pf.sub: Manage your drama series here. Check TikTok reporting, review ad campaigns, or open the US launch priority score to see what needs preparation.
pf.legend: On TikTok = the linked listing has delivered data. Ads active = a campaign is submitted, running or has results. Preparing = neither. Groups can overlap.
pf.col.title: Title
pf.basisGrossNote: GROSS marks a title whose source reports gross purchase sales, not publisher earnings; the two are not comparable.
pf.sort.name: Name
pf.demoNote: Demo dataset: TikTok figures and ad results are simulated and labelled.
promote.new.requirements: Enter a campaign name, a destination link, an audience (at least 3 characters), and a test idea (at least 10 characters) to save.
promote.new.someNoVideo: Titles without video can still save a US campaign brief; generating video ads needs footage.
workflow.noTasks: No campaign needs your action right now. Submitted campaigns are waiting for results.
ws.exp.budgetLater: Budget approval opens at step 4, once the ads are approved.
pf.tiktok.sub: Compare title revenue, viewers and paying-viewer rates. Each row shows its reporting dates; delayed or partial reports may cover different days.
pf.tiktok.emptyHint: Link a listing from a title's TikTok section to start receiving data.
workflow.filter.label: Show
next.summary.mine: Your titles on a top-3 story type
next.tropes.subShort: Share is the percentage of recent listings with this story type. A listing can have several types, so shares can exceed 100% in total. A 1.2× ratio means its share is 20% higher than in the full catalog. Growth is the median change in each listing’s own platform counter across listings with a baseline; small samples may be unrepresentative.
next.tropes.oneLine: Compare the story types in recent listings and changes in their reported views.
review.audienceHint: For example: US women aged 25–44 who watch romance dramas. Minimum 3 characters.
review.hypothesisHint: For example: Will opening with the betrayal get more clicks than opening with the romance? Minimum 10 characters.
review.selectionHint: Selecting adds an ad to this round. Approve ads locks the selected content; budget approval and submission follow separately.
review.sourcePreview: Source footage preview. This player shows the episode, not a finished ad; use the time range below to review the proposed clip.
review.unsavedBrief: You have unsaved changes. Save the brief before approving its budget.
review.noImpressions: Ad {n} has no impressions yet. There is not enough data to judge its performance.
review.resetConfirm: Reset the demo workspace? This replaces locally added titles, campaign changes and sample results with the original demo dataset.
review.materialsIntro: Upload episode files here. The workflow below prepares English subtitles; you can create ads from video without completing subtitle adaptation.
review.noPerformance: No performance data yet. Wait for reported impressions before judging these ads.
promote.workspace.launchDemoNote: Demo dataset: the launch runs against a fake TikTok inside Studio. Nothing is published and nothing is spent.
promote.workspace.launchSandboxNote: TikTok sandbox: objects are created in the sandbox ad account. Nothing is published and nothing is spent.
promote.workspace.launchLiveNote: Pressing launch creates the campaign in your assigned TikTok ad account with the approved budget as its spending ceiling. TikTok reviews the ads before they run.
promote.workspace.renderedPreview: This is the finished ad: the exact file that will be uploaded to TikTok.
promote.workspace.renderPending: Finished video not rendered yet; the source footage is shown.
promote.block.budget_unsigned: the approver must sign the budget
promote.block.budget_below_minimum: the budget must be at least $20 (TikTok's minimum)
promote.block.no_destination: set where viewers should go in the brief
promote.block.unrendered_creatives: every chosen ad needs a finished video; generate the ads again
promote.block.no_launch_account: no TikTok ad account is assigned to your company yet
promote.block.no_identity: the assigned ad account has no TikTok handle linked; Pulsar is on it
promote.launch.title: TikTok launch
promote.new.destinationHint: The link the ad opens: the drama's page on your platform or a web player. TikTok requires it.
workflow.hint.submitted: Created on TikTok. The ads are in TikTok's review; results appear once they run.
workflow.hint.paused: Paused. Nothing is spending until it is switched back on.
workflow.hint.ended: The schedule ended or the budget was spent. Review the results and decide the next round.
ws.launchAccount.title: TikTok launch account
ws.launchAccount.sub: The ad account your campaigns launch into. Pulsar sets it up inside Pulsar's Business Center and assigns it to your company.
ws.launchAccount.noIdentity: No TikTok handle linked yet — Pulsar is completing the setup.
ws.launchAccount.request: Request an ad account from Pulsar
ws.launchAccount.requestSub: Pulsar creates the account and links a publishing handle. You will be able to launch as soon as it is assigned.
ws.launchAccount.paymentSub: Optional. Ad spend on a Pulsar-managed account is billed back to you. Studio records the card brand, holder and last four digits only — never the card number — and charges nothing itself.
ws.launchAccount.sent: Request sent. Pulsar will assign the account.
ws.launchAccount.viewerOnly: An editor or approver can request an account.
admin.promote.launch.paused: Paused on TikTok. Nothing spends until it is resumed.
admin.promote.launch.ended: Ended: schedule closed or budget spent.
admin.promote.launch.synced: Synced: {polled} campaigns polled, {synced} result rows, {errors} errors.
admin.promote.launch.overrideNote: The engine and the scheduler write the normal path. Use this only when TikTok's state and Studio's disagree and you have checked Ads Manager.
admin.promote.launch.notApplied: TikTok accepted the request but did not change state; the next sweep settles it.
admin.tiktok.title: TikTok setup
admin.tiktok.sub: The operator connection to Pulsar's Business Center, the ad accounts it reaches, and which producer each launches from.
admin.tiktok.mode.fake: Fixture: fake TikTok in this process
admin.tiktok.connected: TikTok authorized. The new connection is listed below.
admin.tiktok.redirectUri: Redirect URI to register on the developer app
admin.tiktok.assignTitle: Assign ad account {id} to a producer
admin.tiktok.accountName: Account name shown to the producer
admin.tiktok.identityNone: No handle linked to this ad account — link one in Business Center before assigning, or ads cannot run.
admin.tiktok.scheduler.stopped: Not running in this process (SCHEDULER_DISABLED or no boot hook). Sync now still works.
promote.new.missing: Fill in {fields} to save the brief.
promote.new.field.name: the campaign name
promote.new.field.destinationInvalid: a valid destination link starting with https://
